import pytest
from target import url_basename

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url,expected",
    [
        # Empty and non‑matching inputs
        ("", ""),
        ("not a url", ""),
        ("http://", ""),
        ("http://example.com", ""),
        ("//example.com", ""),

        # Simple single‑segment paths
        ("http://example.com/foo", "foo"),
        ("https://example.com/foo", "foo"),
        ("//example.com/foo", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo?bar=baz", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo#section", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/?q=1", "foo"),

        # Two‑segment paths – both old and new regex give the same result
        ("http://example.com/foo/bar", "bar"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/bar/", "bar"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/bar?x=1", "bar"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/bar#frag", "bar"),

        # Three‑segment paths – this is where the change matters.
        # Old behaviour (spec) should return the last segment.
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c", "c"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c/", "c"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c?x=1", "c"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c#frag", "c"),

        # More than three segments
        ("http://example.com/one/two/three/four", "four"),
        ("http://example.com/one/two/three/four?param=val", "four"),
        ("http://example.com/one/two/three/four#anchor", "four"),

        # Paths that contain characters that were previously allowed in the optional part
        ("http://example.com/segment-with-dash/last", "last"),
        ("http://example.com/segment.with.dot/last", "last"),
        ("http://example.com/segment_with_underscore/last", "last"),
    ],
)
def test_url_basename_returns_expected_basename(url, expected):
    assert url_basename(url) == expected


def test_url_basename_type_is_str():
    # Ensure the return type is a (unicode) string, even for empty input
    result = url_basename("")
    assert isinstance(result, str)


def test_url_basename_handles_trailing_slash_and_query():
    # Combination of trailing slash and query string
    url = "http://example.com/path/to/resource/?key=value"
    assert url_basename(url) == "resource"


def test_url_basename_protocol_relative_url():
    # Protocol‑relative URLs should be handled the same as absolute ones
    url = "//example.com/dir/file"
    assert url_basename(url) == "file"


def test_url_basename_multiple_consecutive_slashes():
    # Multiple slashes in the path should not break the extraction
    url = "http://example.com//double//slashes///file"
    # Old regex treats everything up to the last segment as optional,
    # so the expected basename is still the final non‑empty segment.
    assert url_basename(url) == "file"
